key_idea: Triangulate the polygon and 3-color the resulting graph, ensuring every triangle has one vertex of each color, so the smallest color class covers the polygon.
reason: This is a quintessential 'Book proof' that replaces a complicated geometric argument with a brilliantly simple graph-theoretic insight. The unexpected use of 3-coloring is perfectly explanatory, concise, and makes the bound feel completely inevitable.
recognized: Fisk's proof of the Art Gallery Theorem
